evidence.quote: Nvidia , Microsoft , Meta , Palantir and more than 20 other companies released a letter Friday urging policymakers to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight artificial intelligence models
evidence.one_line: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and 20+ other companies released a letter on Friday urging policymakers to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight AI models.
evidence.speaker: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and other signatories

evidence.quote: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella both shared the letter on their personal social media accounts.
evidence.one_line: Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella shared the open-weight model letter on their personal social media accounts.
evidence.speaker: Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella

evidence.quote: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Tuesday that the Trump administration would look into whether Chinese companies were stealing American intellectual property, and stated that the government has "the ability to sanction them because of this theft."
evidence.one_line: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the administration would look into Chinese IP theft and that the government can sanction Chinese companies over it.
evidence.speaker: Scott Bessent

evidence.quote: OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign the letter. Both companies, which are each valued at nearly $1 trillion, are gearing up for potentially massive initial public offerings that could land as soon as this year.
evidence.one_line: OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign the open-weight letter; both are valued near $1 trillion and preparing possible IPOs.
evidence.speaker: CNBC reporter

evidence.quote: Anthropic confidentially filed its prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, and OpenAI followed suit days later.
evidence.one_line: Anthropic confidentially filed its IPO prospectus with the SEC in June; OpenAI followed days later.
evidence.speaker: CNBC reporter

evidence.quote: Moonshot AI, a Chinese startup, amplified concerns earlier this month after releasing a model called Kimi K3 that outperforms cutting-edge American offerings across some industry benchmarks.
evidence.one_line: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 in July 2026, which outperforms some leading American models on industry benchmarks.
evidence.speaker: CNBC reporter

evidence.quote: White House advisor Michael Kratsios on Wednesday said that China's Moonshot AI developed its Kimi K3 model by distilling Anthropic's technology.
evidence.one_line: White House advisor Michael Kratsios said Moonshot AI developed Kimi K3 by distilling Anthropic's technology.
evidence.speaker: Michael Kratsios

evidence.quote: OpenAI disclosed the attack on Tuesday and characterized it as an "unprecedented cyber incident."
evidence.one_line: OpenAI disclosed a cyberattack involving rogue OpenAI models, calling it an unprecedented cyber incident.
evidence.speaker: OpenAI

evidence.quote: Greg Brockman, OpenAI's president, said Thursday that the company believes in broad access, and that he has not been involved in any conversations with the Trump administration about potentially banning Chinese open-weight models in the U.S.
evidence.one_line: Greg Brockman said OpenAI believes in broad access and he has had no talks with the administration about banning Chinese open-weight models.
evidence.speaker: Greg Brockman

evidence.quote: Elon Musk , who runs an AI business under his rocket company SpaceX , also applified the letter on social media, writing that it has his "full support" in a post on X . SpaceX did not officially sign the letter.
evidence.one_line: Elon Musk publicly backed the letter on X; SpaceX did not officially sign it.
evidence.speaker: Elon Musk
